hints: Focus on the word always. Each wrong option hides one molecule that never contains nitrogen, so look for the carbohydrate or lipid in each list.
Remember the two big nitrogen-containing groups: all proteins have N in amino and peptide bonds, and all nucleic acids have N in their bases. Carbohydrates and most lipids have only C, H and O.
walkthrough:
**Recall who has nitrogen and who does not**

Think in families, not single molecules. Proteins always have N, and nucleic acids always have N in their nitrogenous bases. Carbohydrates like cellulose and starch have only C, H and O, and most lipids also have only C, H and O.

Rule to remember:
$$Carbohydrate = C, H, O \quad Protein = C, H, O, N (+S) \quad Nucleic\ acid = C, H, O, N, P$$

**Use the non-nitrogen molecules to eliminate**

Scan each option for a carbohydrate or a plain lipid. Cellulose in A is a polysaccharide with no N. Most lipids in B have no N. Starch in D is a polysaccharide with no N. Any option containing one of these cannot be correct.

**Check the remaining group**

Enzymes are proteins, so they always contain N in amino acids and peptide bonds. mRNA and tRNA are nucleic acids, so they always contain N in bases like adenine, uracil, cytosine and guanine. All three always contain nitrogen, so C is correct.

options.A: Cellulose is a carbohydrate made only of C, H and O, so it never contains nitrogen even though amino acids and mRNA do.
options.B: Most lipids such as triglycerides contain only C, H and O, so they do not always contain nitrogen even though amino acids and DNA do.
options.C: Enzymes are proteins with nitrogen in every amino acid, and mRNA and tRNA both have nitrogen in their bases, so all three always contain nitrogen.
options.D: Starch is a carbohydrate made only of C, H and O, so it never contains nitrogen even though membrane proteins and tRNA do.
